notes:
CIRCUIT: a hand-drawn 5-row x 6-column ladder/grid. Six vertical columns C1(x~50, left rail), C2(x~208), C3(x~421), C4(x~610), C5(x~800), C6(x~936, right rail); five horizontal rows R1(y~265, top), R2(y~410), R3(y~560), R4(y~725), R5(y~870, bottom). R1 carries five sources in series (V-AC 3V/1kHz #1, I-AC 5A/1kHz #4, V-DC 5V #5, I-DC 10A #9, V-DC 15V #11). R2 carries L 50uH #8 then C 100uF #12; R3 carries L 10uH #6 then C 50uF #10; R4 carries L 5uH #2 then C 10uF #7; R5 carries L 1uH #0 then C 5uF #3. GND #13 hangs off C6 at R3.

DRAFTER'S CONVENTION on this sheet is explicit and consistent: where two runs are NOT connected the row wire makes a U-shaped detour (semicircular jog) below the column; where they ARE connected there is either a fat solder blob (3-5x stroke width in both axes) or the column simply terminates on the row (a T). Verified in the pixels with inkmap at every one of these.

NET MAP (7 nets, 27 terminals):
  n1 = left rail C1 and every row's left-hand run: V-AC left 1.0, L1uH left 0.0, plus R2/R3/R4 left runs which cross C2/C3/C4 without joining, reaching L50uH left 8.0, L10uH left 6.0, L5uH left 2.0.
  n2 = column C2: top-row segment between V-AC and I-AC (1.1, 4.0) and bottom-row segment between L1uH and C5uF (0.1, 3.0). C2 crosses R2, R3, R4 on hops.
  n3 = column C3: top-row segment between I-AC and V-DC5 (4.1, 5.0) and R4 segment between L5uH and C10uF (2.1, 7.1). C3 crosses R2 and R3 on hops.
  n4 = R3 internal node between L10uH right (6.1) and C50uF left (10.1); it crosses C4 on a hop, so no column taps it.
  n5 = R2 internal node between L50uH right (8.1) and C100uF left (12.1); it crosses C5 on a hop.
  n6 = top-rail segment between I-DC right (9.1) and V-DC15 left (11.0). See the judgement call below.
  0  = right rail C6 plus columns C4 and C5 plus the bare-wire right-hand ends of R3 and R4: V-DC5 right 5.1, I-DC left 9.0, C10uF right 7.0, C50uF right 10.0, C100uF right 12.0, V-DC15 right 11.1, C5uF right 3.1, GND 13.0.

PORT FIXES (both are the classic 'terminal landed on the value label' error):
  #7 Capacitor 10uF: t0 was on p3@(511,699), a stroke of the handwritten '10uF' above the symbol (one-terminal net n2 in the tracer output). Repointed t0 -> p0@(526,725), the real right-hand plate lead that runs to S44; t1 stays on p1@(481,728), the left lead running to S45.
  #12 Capacitor 100uF: t0 was on p2@(863,366), a stroke of the handwritten '100uF'. Repointed t0 -> p1@(899,393), the real right-hand lead running to S15 on C6; t1 stays on p0@(851,396), the left lead running left along R2 to the S17 hop.
All other components' ports were checked in the _comps montage and are on the real leads. All 14 classes match the drawn symbols (5 sources, 4 inductors, 4 capacitors, 1 GND); none look mis-classified.

THE ONE UNRESOLVED CONFLICT - S7 (796,264), C5 x R1, recorded as [[18,19],[23]] (top rail passes through; the C5 column top is NOT tied to it):
  Read literally, the ink at S7 is a junction: the C5 column terminates on the top rail and there is a blob there (inkmap: ink from x=783-800, y=259-270 on a 4 px rail). The blob is however centred ~8 px to the LEFT of the column (column at x=798-799), which is more typical of a pen lead-in/lead-out than of a deliberate solder dot centred on the intersection - every other solder dot on this sheet (S10, S29, S30, S44, S45, S54) is centred on its crossing.
  Taking S7 as a junction makes C5 = net 0, because C5 is also tied to net 0 twice over: through the bare-wire right-hand end of R3 (S30 dot -> wire -> S29 dot -> C6) and through the bare-wire right-hand end of R4 (S46 T -> wire -> S43 T -> C6). That puts BOTH terminals of V-DC #11 (15 V) on net 0 - a short-circuited voltage source, an ERC error - and both terminals of I-DC #9 on net 0 as well. I checked every wire on those two paths at pixel level (inkmaps at 801/548, 936/540, 803/727, 936/723 and zooms of the whole right-hand third): the wires are continuous, there is no hop, no gap and no un-annotated component between C5 and C6 on either row. So no single misread crossing explains the short; the drawing itself is degenerate there.
  Per the brief's rule that an electrically impossible reading is the wrong one, I broke the weakest link on that loop, S7, so that the top-rail segment between I-DC and V-DC15 becomes its own net n6 = {9.1, 11.0}. This is the minimum-damage repair: it moves exactly 2 of the 27 terminals relative to the literal reading, and it is the same netlist that the two alternative repairs produce (making S30 and S46 crossings, i.e. leaving C5 a stub, or splitting the C5 column at the S17 hop). It removes the V-DC short and the I-DC short together.
  If an auditor prefers strict ink fidelity, delete the S7 entry from this decisions file: the result is 6 nets with 9.1 and 11.0 folded into net 0, V-DC #11 flagged as short-circuited and I-DC #9 warned. Everything else in this annotation is unchanged either way.
